method: Reviewed supplied official OPR indexes, current local public catalogue and captured biographies; paced anonymous documented WikiTree searchPerson with name variants and all pages for each logged query, then getPeople for plausible historical Open 60/nonliving profiles. Common spouse-name searches use BirthDate=eventyear-25,dateSpread 20,dateInclude=neither; niche no-match names received unrestricted date searches. Privacy-withheld/nameless API rows are counted but not inspected; all reported page offsets were fetched. Some date-filtered API queries return fewer rows than their reported totals; these response-count gaps are recorded without claiming access to omitted profiles. API phonetic matches were manually distinguished from genuine surname forms. No original OPR image inspected, no live writes or new browser.
policy: Loose before birth bounds, other spouses, distant compatible places and missing household bridges alone are not exclusions. Record occurrences are mapped individually; shared-name groups do not establish one life or repeated marriages.
limitations: Original OPR registers are uninspected; index dates do not distinguish banns from completed marriage or death from burial.
Common spouse searches are explicitly bounded and do not establish a global absence of an older or later-born existing profile.
A compatible_candidate link is a qualified existing identity possibility, never a merge, new-profile clearance or certain relationship.
Retained legacy upper-bound candidates are lower-ranked leads; new primary candidates are supported by name, dates and inspected public family context.

Alexander-7545.public_biography:
== Biography ==

===First Marriage to Phillips===


Andrew Alexander married first a dau. of Sir Thomas Phillips, called Governor Phillips, and had a son and heir, Jacob Alexander.  <ref name="burkeland"/> 

Andrew's first wife, a Miss Phillips, was a relative of the Alexanders<ref name="wikical"/>

===Second Marriage to Hilles===

Andrew Alexander married secondly a dau. of the Laird of Hilles, and had a son, John Alexander . . ."<ref name="burkeland"/> 

Andrew's second wife was a Miss Hillhouse<ref name="wikical"/>

===1663 Grant of Lands===

Captain Andrew Alexander of Errigal, County Donegal, forbearer of the Earls of Caledon, was granted lands at Ballyclose near Limavady, County Londonderry in 1663.  <ref name="wikical"> [[Wikipedia: Earl of Caledon]] Accesssed October 30, 2018 [[Day=1904|jhd]] </ref>

===1689 Attainted===

Andrew Alexander was attainted by James II in 1689.  <ref name="burkeland"> Burke's Landed Gentry (1894), p. 16 </ref>

Andrew Alexander was later attainted by the parliament called by James II in Dublin in 1689. <ref name="wikical"/>

===Children===

#Jacob Alexander, son of Andrew and his first wife.  Jacob was the ancestor of the Alexanders of Ahilly (Donegal).<ref name="wikical"/>
#John Alexander, son of Andrew and his second wife, married Anne White, daughter of John White, of Cadyhill, County Londonderry, and had four children, of whom the first, Nathaniel Alexander was born in 1689 and became an Alderman of the city of Derry in 1755 and died on 22 September 1761, having had with other children a third son, James Alexander, who became the 1st Earl of Caledon.<ref name="wikical"/>

==Research Notes==

===1800 Earls of Caledon===

The title Earl of Caledon in the Peerage of Ireland was created 29 December 1800 by George III.  The first holder was James Alexander, 1st Viscount Caledon.  The seat of the barony is Caledon Castle in County Tyrone.  

James Alexander was a merchant who had made an enormous fortune in India. He also represented the constituency of Londonderry City in the Irish House of Commons. Alexander had already been created Baron Caledon in 1790[2] and Viscount Caledon, of Caledon in the County of Tyrone, in 1797,[3] also in the Peerage of Ireland.

James Alexander was succeeded by his son, the second Earl. He was the first Governor of the Cape Colony and sat in the House of Lords as an Irish Representative Peer from 1804 to 1839. His son, the third Earl, briefly represented County Tyrone in the House of Commons as a Tory and was an Irish Representative Peer between 1841 and 1855. His eldest son, the fourth Earl, sat in the House of Lords as an Irish Representative Peer from 1877 to 1898. He was succeeded by his eldest son, the fifth Earl. He never married and was succeeded by his nephew, the 6th Earl. He was the son of the Hon. Herbrand Charles Alexander, second son of the fourth Earl. Today the titles are held by his only son, the seventh Earl, who succeeded in 1980. Lord Caledon was made Lord Lieutenant of County Armagh in 1989.

'''Marion Glasgow''' was born in 1655, recorded as a daughter of William Glasgow; the attachment to [[Glasgow-1556|William Glasgow]] does not by itself prove his identity.<ref name="Baptism1655">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-H5K : 16 September 2021), William Glasgow in entry for Marion Glasgow, 1655.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
An Old Parish Register index records Marion Glasgow and William Glasgow at Kirknewton and East Calder on 10 June 1681.<ref name="Marriage1681">Scotland's People, ''Old Parish Registers: banns and marriages'', index entry for William Glasgow and Marion Glasgow, 10 June 1681, Kirknewton and East Calder, parish 690, reference 10/82, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Scotland’s People] (original image not inspected; supplied reciprocal index entries, reviewed 10 September 2026).</ref> The entry is compatible with this Marion by name, district and age. It does not identify either person's parents or residence, and the combined banns/marriages index cannot prove that 10 June was the wedding date. The original register is needed before attaching the recorded William as a structured spouse.

=== Supplied parish index comparison ===

The supplied Scotland’s People index records '''MARION GLASGOW''' on '''04/11/1655''' at Kirknewton and East Calder, with parent text “WILLIAM GLASGOW/”.<ref name="OPRBirth097">Scotland’s People, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms], exact surname Glasgow through 1700, index text supplied 10 September 2026: MARION GLASGOW, 04/11/1655, WILLIAM GLASGOW/, indexed gender F, Kirknewton and East Calder, parish 690, reference 10 / 37. Original register image not inspected for this review.</ref>

The profile’s structured birth date is 1655-10-11, whereas this index date is 1655-11-04. The two dates remain unreconciled. The combined births and baptisms collection does not establish whether the indexed date is a birthday or a baptism date. A parent’s name alone does not uniquely identify an attached historical person, and the index does not establish an unnamed parent. This date comparison does not resolve the possible later marriage identity discussed above.

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
'''Marion Glasgow''' was the sister of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]], fisher
and burgess of Glasgow. Ninian's 1613 testament left her ten merks and
expressly called her ''his sist[er]''.<ref name="Ninian1613">National Records of
Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, testament of
Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613; working
transcription of the original images supplied 6 September 2026.</ref>

Marion and Robert Fultoun were the parents of [[Fultoun-5|James Fultoun]],
whose Glasgow High Kirk baptism on 7 August 1610 calls him their lawful
son.<ref name="Fultoun1610">Glasgow & West of Scotland Family History Society,
''Glasgow High Kirk Baptisms 1609–1777'', vol. 1/320, 7 August 1610, James
Fultoun, lawful son of Robert Fultoun and Marion Glasgow; witnesses John Howie
and James Barr,
[https://www.gwsfhs.org.uk/records/james-fultoun/ public index].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

Marion is Ninian's sister and is confidently identified as a daughter of
[[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]]. Ninian's burgess admission on 23 October 1596
calls him Robert Glasgow's second son; his 1613 testament expressly calls
Marion his sister.<ref>James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of
Glasgow, 1573–1750'' (Scottish Record Society, 1925),
[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24],
23 October 1596, Ninian Glasgow, second son to Robert Glasgow, fisher,
burgess.</ref><ref name="Ninian1613" /> Together with their shared Glasgow
surname and compatible chronology, these records support the common father.
No evidence identifies a different father for Marion. The existing birth entry is a before-1592 boundary, not evidence that Marion was born in 1592. This is a confident
inference from the combined records, rather than an express father-daughter
statement. Her mother is not identified; the currently attached mother remains
uncertain.

Jonet Meik's 1607 testament also names Marion as a legatee but does not call
her a daughter.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court,
CC9/7/5, images 82–83, testament of Jonet Meik.</ref>

[[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]] named a daughter Marion in his
1597/8 testament.<ref name="Andrew1598">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh
Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory
of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8 and confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected
working transcription of the original register images.</ref> Shared name and
chronology do not identify this profile as that daughter. No record connects
The Fultoun household to Andrew, Elizat Stevinsoun, Corsoun or Andrew's land,
while Ninian's direct statement that this Marion was his sister establishes a
substantial competing family context. This profile is not the present match;
do not attach Andrew without an identity bridge. [[Glasgow-4095|The testament-named Marion of Corsoun]] has a separate profile while the identity remains unproved.

Marion was named as a legatee in the 1607 testament of Jonet Meik, wife of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]], but the testament does not describe Marion as their daughter. Ninian's 1613 testament proves their sibling relationship; the currently attached [[Meik-14|Jonet Meik]] mother relationship remains uncertain.

An earlier profile note mentioned [[Glasgow-992|William Glasgow]] and [[Howie-1119|Bessie Howie]]. That association does not identify Marion's father or change the direct 1610 evidence naming James Fultoun as her son and Robert Fultoun as the child's father.

Further research should search Glasgow sasines and testaments for Marion Glasgow or Robert Fultoun naming a maternal relative.

Glasgow-3143.public_biography:
== Biography ==

'''Marion Glasgow''' was baptised at Edinburgh on 29 January 1657, a daughter of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow (1626-)]], weaver, and '''[[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]]'''.<ref name="MarionBaptism">“Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', Marione Glesgow, baptised 29 January 1657, Edinburgh, daughter of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1YD-PR2 record X1YD-PR2].</ref>

=== Marriage ===

Marion married '''William Calder''' at Edinburgh on 29 June 1686.<ref name="MarionMarriage">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Marion; William Calder 29 June 1686.”</ref>

On 30 June 1686, the day after their marriage, William was admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh. The entry describes him as a weaver and states that his admission was by right of his wife Marion, daughter of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess.<ref name="CalderBurgess">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=101 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 91: “Calder, Wm., B., weaver, be r. of w. Marion, dr. to James Glasgow, weaver, B. 30 June 1686.”</ref>

This entry directly establishes both Marion's marriage to William Calder and her relationship to her father.

Marion's date and place of death have not been identified.

== Research Notes ==

=== Parentage ===

Marion's baptism names James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan as her parents.<ref name="MarionBaptism" />

William Calder's burgess admission independently identifies Marion as a daughter of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess of Edinburgh.<ref name="CalderBurgess" />

The father named in these records was the Edinburgh weaver apprenticed in 1641 and admitted as a burgess in 1649. He was distinct from the James Glasgow baptised at Inveresk in 1626 as a son of Alexander Glasgow.

=== Name and date ===

The baptismal index records her name as “Marione Glesgow.” The later marriage and burgess records use the form Marion Glasgow.

The baptism dated 29 January 1657 is Marion's record. It is not evidence for a son named James Glasgow born on that date.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original 1657 baptism entry;
* William Calder's apprenticeship and incorporation records;
* baptismal records for any children of Marion and William;
* property or burgess records concerning the Calder household;
* testaments for Marion, William or their parents; and
* burial records for Marion and William.

== Biography ==
'''Thomas Glasgow''' was born before about 1627, probably in Scotland. His
exact birth date, birthplace and parents have not been established. Edinburgh
is a reasonable uncertain location from his documented adult household there,
but not a recorded place of birth.

Thomas and '''[[Weir-3979|Catharine Weir]]''' were the parents of four children
recorded in Edinburgh:

|-

|}<ref name="Children">Edinburgh parish register index entries preserved on
The live profiles: Margaret Glasgow, 27 December 1644, Thomas Glasgow/Catharine
Weir, OPR 685/1, FR1323; Elizabeth Glasgow, 1 July 1647, OPR 685/1, FR1362;
Catharine Glasgow, 16 January 1649, OPR 685/1, FR1400; and Jeane Glasgow, 8
March 1650, OPR 685/1, FR1426.</ref>

The first child's date shows that Thomas and Catharine were together by
December 1644. The profile's 1644 marriage date is therefore an estimate, not
an identified marriage entry.

On 2 May 1660 Thomas was admitted as a burgess and guild brother of Edinburgh,
gratis.<ref name="Burgess1660">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed.,
[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=219
''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record
Society, 1929), printed p. 209: “Glasgow, Thos., B. and G., gratis”, 2 May
1660; see also Findmypast,
[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FBURGESS%2F1009527&tab=this
SCOT/BURGESS/1009527], captured 3 September 2026.</ref> The word “gratis” means
that the entry does not supply the usual apprenticeship- or marriage-right; it
does not identify Thomas's occupation or relatives.

Thomas's death date and place have not been identified. He was alive on 2 May
1660.<ref name="Burgess1660" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

==== Identification with the burgess ====
The 1660 burgess is probably this Thomas. The exact name, city and adult
chronology continue the Edinburgh household documented between 1644 and 1650.
The admission lacks a wife, trade or kinship statement, so the identification
should remain explicitly probable.

==== Parentage ====
Thomas is attached to [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] and [[Mathie-159|Jonet
Mathie]]. No birth or baptism record inspected for Thomas names those parents.
The child records and burgess admission establish his adult Edinburgh identity
but do not prove that attachment. Preserve the relationships as uncertain
working hypotheses unless direct evidence is found.

==== Thomas M.A. ====
[[Glasgow-3413|Thomas Glasgow M.A.]] graduated from the University of Edinburgh
on 20 March 1670.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/catalogueofgr10600univuoft/page/100/mode/2up
''A Catalogue of the Graduates in the Faculties of Arts, Divinity, and Law of
The University of Edinburgh''], printed p. 100.</ref> He is attached as a son
of this household, but the university entry supplies no father and shared
city/name evidence is insufficient. Keep that relationship uncertain.

Thomas's wife [[Weir-3979|Catharine Weir]] should not be confused with
[[Glasgow-1495|Catharine Glasgow]], wife of a Thomas Weir. The broader
same-name comparison is maintained at
[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Thomas-1 Thomas Research].

* [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Thomas-1 Thomas Research]
* His wife, [[Weir-3979|Catherine (Weir) Glasgow (abt.1625-)]] is not to be confused with [[Glasgow-1495|Catherine (Glasgow) Weir (bef.1584-)]]

== Biography ==

'''Marion Glasgow''' was a daughter of [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]]. Andrew's testament, made on 6 February 1597/8, provides that if his wife Elizat Stevinsoun was not pregnant, his third was to be divided among “his said sone and his said [dochter… struck through] Marione, Jonet, Isobell.”<ref name="Andrew1598">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected working transcription of the original register images. Printed index: Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108].</ref>

Her brother [[Glasgow-4006|Robert]] is expressly called Andrew's son by Elizat. The testament does not separately state that Elizat was this daughter's mother, so maternity should not be inferred as certain from this clause alone.<ref name="Andrew1598"/>

== Research Notes ==

=== Identity ===

Named as a lawful daughter in Andrew's 1598 testament. No later record has been securely connected to her; the same-name Glasgow women of the period have no Corsoun, Stevenson, sibling or succession bridge to this household, so none is attached here.

A separate [[Glasgow-3062|Marion Glasgow]] is identified as [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]'s sister in his 1613 testament and as the mother of James Fultoun in a 1610 Glasgow baptism. Neither record names Andrew, Elizat or Corsoun. This is a same-name identity comparison, not a proved match; keep the profiles separate pending a connecting record.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, Ninian Glasgow testament; Glasgow & West of Scotland Family History Society, [https://www.gwsfhs.org.uk/records/james-fultoun/ James Fultoun baptism index], 7 August 1610.</ref>

Glasgow-4151.public_biography:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

'''Agnes Glasgow''' was a lawful child of [[Glasgow-4152|John Glasgow]], a sailor in Saltcoats
within Ardrossan parish. She and [[Glasgow-4153|Katherine Glasgow]] were named in their
father's testament dative and inventory when his estate came before Glasgow
Commissary Court in April 1637. Their father had died in December 1636.<ref name="JohnTestament">National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court,
testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, NRS
CC9/7/27, register pp. 478–480; death in December 1636 and court proceedings in
April 1637; original register re-read September 2026; locate by reference
through the [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills
Scotland's People wills search].</ref>

The proceeding calls Agnes and Katherine the lawful children of the deceased,
their father. It names '''Isobell Gray''' as John's widow and records that she
gave up the inventory on the children's behalf. This proves Agnes's father and
Isobell's marriage to him, but does not expressly call Isobell Agnes's
mother.<ref name="JohnTestament" />

== Research Notes ==

The testament does not state Agnes's age, birthplace, marriage or death.
Saltcoats is an uncertain creation-field birthplace inferred from her father's
residence, not a stated fact. The document's use of ''bairn'' proves a
parent-child relationship; it does not by itself establish that Agnes was a
young child in 1637.

[[Glasgow-1030]] has been excluded as the present identity of her father: his
documented Glasgow-burgh household has no Saltcoats, sailor, Isobell Gray,
Katherine or Agnes bridge. Create the distinct Saltcoats John first and attach
Agnes to that new profile with certain status. No mother should be attached
merely because Isobell Gray was John's widow and acted for the children.

Reid-24609.public_biography: == Biography == ==Birth== John Reid was born in Edinburgh, Scotland the son of William Reid.Scotland's People, Old Parish Registers, Births and Baptisms. https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/church-registers/church-births-baptisms Accessed 3 September 2024. Note that FreeReg.uk does not have Midlothian births transcribed as of this date. Two baptismal records were found in Scotland's People for John Reid as son of William: on 4 March 1598 and on 17 October 1602, recorded in Edinburgh Parish (St. Giles Cathedral). No mothers were given in his birth record, so it is unclear at this time which one is for John Reid who married Helen Henderson. They were direct relations of William Reid who married Janet Cochrane on 10 October 1599. This William was considered a merchant elite.Brown, James J. THE SOCIAL, POLITICAL AND ECONOMIC INFLUENCES OF THE EDINBURGH MERCHANT ELITE, 1600-1638 https://era.ed.ac.uk/handle/1842/6860 Vol. 2, p. 516. Accessed 3 September 2024. Patrick Cochrane was his father-in-law.Brown. Vol. 1, p. 51 Accessed 3 September 2024. William served on the Edinburgh Burgess with Mungo McCall [aka Mackall and variations].Brown. Vol. 1, p. 66 Accessed 3 September 2024. ==Residence== The family lived in the Lawnmarket section of the High Street, and on the northside of the High Street in what was known as Bailie Reid's Close. It is located about 1.5 blocks west of St. Giles Cathedral, between Baxter's Close on the west and Jameson's Close on the east. Note that Lawnmarket is the part of High Street where linen (also known as lawn) was sold. The complex contained both a home and tenements as well as a shop where perhaps John and his father sold their linen. The land of John Ronald lay on the north side of the High Street, in Ronald's, or Bailie Reid's Close. It may be that John became a merchant of linen after beginning his work as a weaver. Or, it may be that John was not buried in Edinburgh. One William Reid, a weaver, was buried at the east end of the kirk in Greyfriars on 24 April 1685."Edinburgh [Scotland], Kirk of the Greyfriars, Greyfriars' Churchyard, Henry Paton, Scottish Record Society"Greyfriars Burying Ground, Edinburgh p. 541 https://archive.org/details/registerinterme00socigoog Accessed 27 September 2024. ==Notes== The church which serves Edinburgh Parish is St. Giles Cathedral,St. Giles Cathedral History https://www.stgilescathedral.org.uk/history Accessed 28 September 2024. located on the High Street. Because of the lack of space for burials, the members were buried in Greyfriars Kirkyard (burying ground) beginning in 1562 with most of the interments after 1600.Greyfriars Kirkyard https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greyfriars_Kirkyard Accessed 28 September 2024. == Sources ==
